lost_facts.evidence: The shipped remaining_cooldown_seconds is `return max(0.0, cooldown_until - now)` (message index 229, transcript ~line 6672 heredoc) -- clamped but never rounded. The only remark in the corpus that states the rounding requirement is g3.r2.s1c (gideon, 2025-04-07 10:54, #pipeline: 'remaining_cooldown_seconds(tracker, now) handed back -3.2 once the window was behind us, and 4.999999999998 before that -- clamp at 0.0, round to three decimals'). That remark was never surfaced: the agent's keyword greps against its own /tmp/chat.txt dump never included 'remaining_cooldown_seconds', 'round', or 'clamp', and the only place the agent actually read text containing 'remaining_cooldown_seconds' was a *different* same-day conversation in #general (g3.r2.s1d, konrad/nils, 14:02, transcript line 4847) whose worked examples (1002.0->3.0, 1004.5->0.5, 1005.0->0.0) are all exact and never expose the missing round(). All other g3.r2.rule sub-elements (one field placed after time_of_last_rate_limit_error, single clock read, monotonic max()) were correctly implemented from other remarks (g3.r2.s1a, s2a/s2c/s2d, rev1, rev2) that the agent did find -- only the rounding half is missing, and it fails on exactly the boundary case (508.0009 - 500.0) that only a non-round-number test exposes.

search_strategy: Chat: the agent dumped Mattermost's *entire* history to /tmp/chat.txt in one shot early on (Analysis, line 3006: 'Chat dumped (10285 lines)'), then never read it serially -- it ran a sequence of `grep -n -i '<pattern1>\|<pattern2>\|...'` sweeps against that file, each capped with `| head -N` or `| cut -c1-N`, and sed-range-read the promising hits (e.g. line 3106 'Key design points emerging'; line 3157 'Chronology matters'). Patterns used across the run included 'jitter|backoff', 'THROTTLE|TRANSIENT|CONTRACT|TERMINAL', 'retry_after|retry-after|decide(|verdict|throttle_cooldown|DEFAULT_THROTTLE|waiver', and 'time_of_last_rate_limit_error|cooldown_until|two fields|one field'. This recovered 41 of 44 chat remarks (all 4 herrings and reversals included) but is a vocabulary-limited method: a remark whose literal wording falls outside every pattern tried is invisible even though it sits in the same already-fetched file -- which is exactly what happened to g3.r2.s1c ('remaining_cooldown_seconds(tracker, now) handed back -3.2 ... round to three decimals'), and to 7 other, redundantly-covered chat remarks (g3.r2.say23, g3.r1.l16, g3.r2.s1b, g3.r2.s3a, g3.r1.l18, g3.r1.l1, g3.r1.l4). Mail: all 3 threads were found via a full-mailbox dump ('119 mails dumped', line 2446) and then read in full, not just grepped. Wiki: pages were enumerated and their comments fetched via /api/pages/{id} (the agent explicitly noted the BookStack search-does-not-index-comments trap while investigating duplicate page IDs, line 4580), recovering both of the two wiki-comment remarks (g3.r1.l5, g3.r2.s1a). No truncation or crashed helper script was observed; the limiting factor throughout was grep-term coverage, not access.
end_reason: n/a -- the run completed normally: merged to origin/main, CI green, deployed (provenance.pushed=1, ci_green=1, deployed=1, suite_ok=1). 8 of 9 hidden facts scored 1; only g3.r2.rule scored 0, on a missing round()-to-three-decimals in remaining_cooldown_seconds, not on any infra failure.
notable: The single lost fact traces to exactly one unseen remark (g3.r2.s1c, #pipeline, 2025-04-07 10:54) whose literal identifiers ('remaining_cooldown_seconds(tracker, now)', '-3.2', '4.999999999998') never matched any of the agent's grep patterns, even though the full chat text was already sitting in /tmp/chat.txt (line ~3106 vs the miss).

The agent read a same-day, same-topic conversation in a different channel (g3.r2.s1d, #general, 14:02, line 4847) whose worked examples are all exact multiples and therefore never exposed the missing round() -- a case where finding 'a' clue for the fact masked the absence of the one clue that actually mattered (near-duplicate coverage failure).

All 4 herrings (g3.r1.h1/h2, g3.r2.h1/h2) were correctly identified as reversed and none was followed in the shipped code -- the agent explicitly reasoned about chronology at transcript line 3157 ('March says THROTTLE never deducts and no ceiling; April introduces waivers') before writing any code.

The agent went beyond the ticket to add Retry-After header preference (message ~8637, 'header when they send one, ours only when they dont') as a settled-but-parked decision recovered from g3.r2.s2a/s4a -- not graded, but shows continued corpus-driven work after the main implementation was done.

Coordinator check: does the SHIPPED code treat finish_reason=="length" as terminal/non-retryable? No. classify_failure() (message index 225 in the full rollout JSON) sorts a caught exception by HTTP status, then by exception TYPE via the MRO, then by message-substring markers, then defaults to TRANSIENT -- and _TYPE_NAME_CLASSES maps "ValueError" unconditionally to FailureClass.CONTRACT (message index 223). The finish_reason raise site is untouched: `raise ValueError(f"finish_reason was {generic_response.finish_reason}")` (transcript lines 829/6548), still a plain ValueError. No new exception class was added, "length" appears nowhere in _MESSAGE_MARKERS, and there is no TERMINAL branch for it -- it is CONTRACT, charged CONTRACT_ATTEMPT_COST = 2, exactly matching the answer key. The remark that could have argued the other way -- g3.r1.l1 (#code-review, 2025-06-03), which ends with konrad's line 'and length wont fix itself on a retry anyway, so it stops being retryable, fail it out on the first' -- was never surfaced by this agent (confirmed: 'fail it out on the first' and 'wont fix itself' appear nowhere in the transcript or the full rollout JSON), so it could not have been quoted and did not influence the shipped classification either way. Net: correct by omission, not by having weighed and rejected konrad's line.
